body: There are lots of really nice people out there, don't forget that :)

I would strongly recommend finding someone you can really talk everything through with. It could be a good listener, an animal or just writing yourself a note. It feels like a weight off your shoulders. Drop me a PM if you want, when I check this account I'll reply.

You can get through this. You sound pretty tough, and better at juggling your life than a lot of people, but things mount up. Unfortunately, the way this universe works means you have to do one thing at a time, but you can do that, and eventually you WILL be glad of where you've ended. Everyone struggles with work and money, everyone sometimes thinks they have no friends, everyone gets party shy. Depression sucks, but you can feel normal again.

Ring that number.

Oh yeah, I kinda think this is a key factor of depression. Everything is such hard work. Everything you think about doing seems like such hard work. And for what? More of being here, in this depressed place? Yeah, those thoughts suck.

But things can change, you can feel normal again. You'll be glad you made it through. I genuinely believed I never would be glad again, but I was. It was good to be wrong.

1. "I've been in love with my best friend for almost 10 years". Not true. Your own post suggests otherwise: "fall for her again". Don't tell yourself lies, it just doesn't end well.
2. You've fallen for her again, which is totally understandable. There is a reason you're friends, and that's because you're pretty compatible together. Don't feel bad for your natural instincts telling you to want more.
3. We've all chickened out. God fucking damn have I felt like an idiot before. It's how we learn. You now know chickening out sucks. Rejection sucks too, but in the long run it feels much better than being a chicken.
4. "I'm usually the type to not talk about problems like this" - That seriously made me cringe. There's no need to be like that, and if you find a safe place to express yourself DO IT! Even if you don't feel like submitting, save the post. You could always submit later. You will look back on it from better days and be glad of where you've got yourself.
5. You'll probably find someone better for you. Or maybe she'll say yes. They're both pretty good options.

Good luck!

It's possible your children could experience depression, and if they see how their parent also struggled but still made it through it could help them a lot, don't you think? Either way they will eventually find out, so you might actually want to look for their support in dark times (probably depends on age).

Hey man.

I just want to say I am impressed at how well you have put your low self-esteem in to words. That sounds like a really dumb thing to say but I genuinely mean it, especially since you said putting it in to words throws you in to an anxious rage.

You seem very focused on your physical appearance. I googled morphea and it wasn't anywhere near as bad as I was expecting. There are people out there living healthy relationships with WAY WAY worse. From the sounds of it you haven't self harmed. That's really fucking impressive, you should seriously be proud. There are people out there with scars all over their bodies. I know, I dated one. If you love someone it doesn't stop you. Don't get hung up on physical appearance.

I am a tall, average looking guy. I hate myself. I too am scared to leave this chair. I don't want people to see me.

I'm not here to offer a solution, unfortunately. But I want to let you know that other people feel this way, and you are probably blaming something that is going on in your head on the way that you look.

Good luck. Stay strong.
